sections.h2: When is Kingsport property tax due, and is it past due now?
sections.html:
Kingsport city tax is due by November 30 each year, and today is November 15, 2026, so a 2026 city bill is still payable on time for another two weeks. Anything unpaid becomes delinquent on December 1. The city's property tax page sets the penalties: 2% on December 1, another 2% on January 1, and 1% for each month after that until the bill is paid.

City statements are mailed between mid September and mid October, once the state approves the assessments, and values are set as of January 1. Payments can be mailed, put in the night deposit box, or made at the Customer Service Center in City Hall at 415 Broad Street. Questions go to 423-343-9860.

The county bill is a separate calendar. The Sullivan County Trustee says county tax is due the first Monday in October and can be paid without penalty through the last day of February. A Kingsport homeowner can therefore be holding a November 30 city deadline and a February county deadline at the same time.

sections.h2: Who handles Kingsport property tax besides City Hall?
sections.html:
The Sullivan County Property Assessor sets the value, and the Sullivan County Trustee collects the county portion. The Trustee's FAQ lists a main office at 1651 Blountville Boulevard in Blountville, 423-323-6464, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. A Kingsport satellite office at 225 West Center Street, Suite 101, takes payments Monday through Wednesday from October 1 to March 15 at 423-354-7036, and it closes from mid March through September.

Kingsport also reaches into Hawkins County, so a house in that part of the city belongs to the Hawkins County assessor and trustee. Ask the Hawkins County Trustee for that county's own dates and rate.

Sullivan County also posts these points for taxpayers:

  • The county mails a courtesy notice, but Tennessee does not require one
  • Installments are allowed between October 1 and February 28, and the owner tracks the balance
  • Cards carry a 2.5% fee and e-checks a $1.25 fee
  • Interest runs at 1.5% per month from March 1, and payment is accepted through March 15 before the account moves to the Clerk and Master

sections.h2: What are the Kingsport and Sullivan County tax rates?
sections.html:
The City of Kingsport lists a 2025 rate of $1.67 per $100 of assessed value, down from $1.99 for 2024. Sullivan County's FAQ gives a 2025 county rate of $1.6129. The city explains the change: the state's two-year ratio appraisal cost Kingsport about $3.8 million a year in revenue, Sullivan County reassessed in 2025 for the first time since 2021, and the city's fiscal 2026 budget took effect July 1.

Here is how the arithmetic works for a house appraised at $200,000. Residential property is assessed at 25%, so the assessment is $50,000. At the city rate that gives $835, and at the county rate it gives about $806. These are illustrations only; the rates on your own notice control.

sections.h2: What is Kingsport like for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Kingsport lies along the Holston River in western Sullivan County and extends into Hawkins County and north to the Virginia line. It sits where U.S. 11W and U.S. 23 meet, and it is the northwest end of Interstate 26. The city covers about 51 square miles and was chartered in 1822, then re-chartered in 1917 when it adopted the council-manager system it still uses.

Eastman Chemical Company has its headquarters and first plant in the city, much of it on Long Island in the Holston. Domtar runs a recycled containerboard mill, and the Holston Army Ammunition Plant manufactures explosives for the Department of Defense. Kingsport City Schools serve almost every resident, with Dobyns-Bennett High School as the main high school. Neighborhoods include Lynn Garden, Bloomingdale, Colonial Heights, Rock Springs, Highland Park and Orebank, among others.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for Kingsport:

  • 57,530 residents on July 1, 2025, up 3.6% from April 2020
  • Owner-occupied rate of 60.1% and 25,021 households
  • Median owner-occupied home value of $234,100 for 2020 to 2024
  • Median gross rent of $907 and median household income of $52,490
  • 23.3% of residents are 65 or older, the highest share among the places compared

The city and the state both run relief programs aimed at senior and disabled owners, covered below.

sections.h2: How does a Kingsport owner dispute a higher value?
sections.html:
Values follow a yearly cycle that the Tennessee assessment calendar spells out. Ownership and condition are fixed as of January 1, change notices are due out by May 20, and the county board of equalization meets from June 1 through the month. Because Sullivan County reassessed in 2025, many Kingsport owners saw a new number that year, and the 2026 appeal window has already closed for most of them.

The next steps for someone who disagrees with a value:

  • Call the Sullivan County Assessor before the next June board meeting and ask whether an informal review is offered
  • File with the county board of equalization, since skipping it generally ends later appeal rights
  • Gather sales of similar Kingsport houses, with differences in age, condition and size explained
  • Pay the undisputed part of the bill on time while the dispute is open

sections.h2: Are there relief programs for Kingsport homeowners?
sections.html:
The city notes that a relief program exists for elderly or disabled homeowners within income limits, and links a brochure and the state Comptroller's relief page. Sullivan County states it does not offer a Tax Freeze program, so relief is the route there. A relief voucher for an owner with a mortgage must be signed and returned by April 5 each year or the state voids the credit.

For the dispute process, the state's appeal rules start at the county board of equalization, and the Sullivan Assessor can say when it sits.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Kingsport house with the tax unpaid?
sections.html:
Sullivan County's guidance is that the owner of record on January 1 gets the notice, and a buyer who closes later is still responsible for making sure tax is paid on time. The settlement statement is where the split is written down. If the November 30 city deadline passes before closing, the city penalty and the county interest grow every month, so a payoff request should be dated close to the closing day.

Unpaid tax is settled from the seller's proceeds at the table. Call the city at 423-343-9860 and the Trustee in Blountville for written payoffs.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the November 30 Kingsport deadline?
faqs.a: A 2% penalty applies on December 1, another 2% on January 1, and 1% each month after until you pay. Mail, the night deposit box and the City Hall counter at 415 Broad Street are all accepted.

faqs.q: Is the Kingsport city rate going up or down?
faqs.a: The 2025 city rate is $1.67 per $100, lower than the $1.99 listed for 2024. The city ties the shift to the state's ratio appraisal and the 2025 Sullivan County reassessment.

faqs.q: Where do I pay the Sullivan County part of my Kingsport tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Sullivan County Trustee in Blountville or at the Kingsport satellite office on West Center Street, which is open Monday through Wednesday from October 1 to March 15. Online and phone payments add card or e-check fees.

faqs.q: Does Kingsport have a tax freeze for seniors?
faqs.a: Sullivan County says it does not offer a Tax Freeze program. The state tax relief program is available for eligible elderly and disabled owners, and the voucher goes back by April 5.

faqs.q: Can a Kingsport house with unpaid taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid city and county balances are paid from the seller's proceeds at closing. Get written payoff figures from the city and the county Trustee before the closing date.
